A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GraspCoT study, with readable methods, equations, six figures and five result tables. All 11 pages of each were inspected. Neither contains an appendix; supplementary material is referenced but not embedded.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 report original IntentGrasp evaluations, component ablations and real-world Kinova Gen3 grasping experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains the original benchmark results, ablations and robot grasping success rates in Tables 1–5.

M1.justification: The visual encoding, three-stage physical-property CoT, masked descriptor supervision, grasp prediction heads, Hungarian matching and training losses remain unchanged. No different algorithmic procedure is specified.

E1.justification: Both versions use IntentGrasp and the same real-world scenarios: explicit instructions and flexible instructions requiring single-target or sequential multi-target grasping. No dataset, domain or task scenario is added.

E2.justification: 3DAPNet and LGrasp6D remain the external baselines in Table 1. The same comparisons with GraspCoT without CoT are retained throughout. The additional related-work citations are not evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: The 80/20 split, 600 evaluated poses per scene, CR thresholds, training settings and robot success-rate protocol are retained. The new EW-CFR equation documents an already-used metric; the PDFs do not report a changed evaluation calculation.

E4.justification: Both contain the same physical-property/action ablations, single-versus-multiple-target breakdown, two-to-five-view sensitivity study and qualitative grasping examples. No additional analysis is presented in v2.

E5.justification: Both report 35 repeated real-world grasping experiments per setting. Seed information, uncertainty intervals, error bars and significance tests remain absent.

E6.justification: All entries in Tables 1–5 and the qualitative examples are retained. For example, GraspCoT's Table 1 CR@0.2, EMD and EW-CFR remain 0.5587, 0.2520 and 0.4229; Table 5 success rates remain 54.2%, 54.2% and 46.7%.

T1.justification: Section 4.1 adds Equation 3, explicitly defining the custom EW-CFR metric through a binary collision check and normalized EMD weighting. v1 describes this combination only verbally. The task definitions and loss equation are unchanged, and no proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: physical-property-oriented CoT, a unified multimodal grasping framework, the IntentGrasp benchmark and superior benchmark and real-world performance.

C2.justification: The interpretations of CoT benefits and view-count saturation are unchanged. Both retain the slender-object grasping limitation and the proposed extension to dynamic scenes using sequential video.

D1.justification: v2 replaces the future code/data-release promise with a concrete code-repository link, specifies the EW-CFR computation and adds a supplementary-video pointer. The pruning description drops the word 'clustering' without specifying a replacement procedure. Hardware and hyperparameters remain unchanged; data release is no longer explicitly promised.

R1.justification: Section 2 adds citations to AffordanceLLM and Grasp as You Say, listed as references 31 and 46 in v2. The research positioning remains intact. Venue updates for existing references do not introduce additional works.

P1.justification: v2 condenses the real-world setup description, makes limited wording and notation edits, separates the limitations paragraph and adds funding acknowledgments. The section organization and most prose are retained.

P2.justification: Table 4 moves from page 7 to page 8, Figure 6 gains a supplementary-video note, and spacing and pagination change. The six figures and five tables retain their substantive visual content and structure.

improvement.justification: The explicit EW-CFR definition and concrete code-access information modestly improve transparency and reproducibility documentation without changing the scientific evidence. These gains are limited: Equation 3 still leaves the normalization choice unspecified, and the abstract no longer explicitly promises data release.
